scenario.summary: Threat actors use passkey and SSO-themed social engineering to lure victims into AiTM or device-code phishing flows, resulting in cloud identity compromise. Once access is gained, they establish persistence by registering new MFA methods and use Microsoft Graph for large-scale reconnaissance and exfiltration of SharePoint, OneDrive, and email data.

meta.rationale: The hunt begins by scoping to endpoints running Microsoft 365/Office software using hb_software_inventory to ensure we are looking at the relevant user population. It then focuses on the behavioral sequence of accessing 'reconnaissance' portals like My Apps and Approval Management.
meta.hypothesis: An adversary is using a compromised identity to systematically enumerate M365 applications and sensitive document repositories, likely using automated tools to collect and exfiltrate data following a passkey-themed phishing event.

hunt.name: M365 Cloud Reconnaissance and Automated Data Collection
hunt.description: This hunt focuses on post-compromise activity following passkey-themed social engineering. Attackers use automated tools (often Node.js-based) to traverse the Microsoft Graph, hitting 'My Apps', 'My Sign-Ins', and 'Microsoft Approval Management' to discover the victim's reach. This is followed by high-volume file enumeration and access in SharePoint and OneDrive. We first identify the estate running Office/M365 software, detect anomalous discovery portal sequences, and then parallelize evidence collection across resource prevalence, file volume, and DNS indicators.

It then focuses on the behavioral sequence of accessing 'reconnaissance' portals like My Apps and Approval Management.
config.beyond_detection: A single rule could flag 'My Apps' access, but this hunt identifies intent by correlating the sequence of discovery portal hits, the stack-count prevalence (baseline), and the volume of subsequent SharePoint access — context a single alert cannot provide.

config.content: SELECT device_hostname, package_name, vendor_name FROM hb_software_inventory WHERE (LOWER(package_name) LIKE '%microsoft%365%' OR LOWER(package_name) LIKE '%office%') AND (LOWER(vendor_name) LIKE '%microsoft%')
config.description: Identify hosts with Microsoft 365 or Office installations to define the relevant estate for cloud identity compromise.
config.expected_signal: A list of hosts that use M365. Silence means the software inventory is either empty or does not contain these packages.

primitive_config.label: Scope Estate for M365/Office Users
primitive_config.content: SELECT device_hostname, package_name, vendor_name FROM hb_software_inventory WHERE (LOWER(package_name) LIKE '%microsoft%365%' OR LOWER(package_name) LIKE '%office%') AND (LOWER(vendor_name) LIKE '%microsoft%')
primitive_config.expected: A list of hosts that use M365. Silence means the software inventory is either empty or does not contain these packages.

config.content: SELECT actor_user_name, src_endpoint_ip, GROUP_CONCAT(DISTINCT dst_endpoint_name) as portals_accessed, COUNT(DISTINCT dst_endpoint_name) as portal_count, MIN(time) as start_time, MAX(time) as end_time FROM hb_auth_signin WHERE status_id = 1 AND instr(',' || '{{discovery_portals}}' || ',', ',' || LOWER(dst_endpoint_name) || ',') > 0 AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days') GROUP BY actor_user_name, src_endpoint_ip HAVING portal_count >= 3
config.description: Find users accessing multiple sensitive identity and application portals in a short window, suggesting automated cloud discovery.
config.expected_signal: Users hitting 3+ distinct discovery portals. High portal counts in short windows are a strong indicator of automated reconnaissance.

primitive_config.label: Reconnaissance Portal Sequence Detection
primitive_config.content: SELECT actor_user_name, src_endpoint_ip, GROUP_CONCAT(DISTINCT dst_endpoint_name) as portals_accessed, COUNT(DISTINCT dst_endpoint_name) as portal_count, MIN(time) as start_time, MAX(time) as end_time FROM hb_auth_signin WHERE status_id = 1 AND instr(',' || '{{discovery_portals}}' || ',', ',' || LOWER(dst_endpoint_name) || ',') > 0 AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days') GROUP BY actor_user_name, src_endpoint_ip HAVING portal_count >= 3
primitive_config.expected: Users hitting 3+ distinct discovery portals. High portal counts in short windows are a strong indicator of automated reconnaissance.

config.content: SELECT dst_endpoint_name, COUNT(DISTINCT actor_user_name) as users, MIN(time) as first_seen FROM hb_auth_signin WHERE status_id = 1 AND instr(',' || '{{discovery_portals}}' || ',', ',' || LOWER(dst_endpoint_name) || ',') > 0 AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days') GROUP BY dst_endpoint_name ORDER BY users ASC
config.description: Stack-count users per portal to identify which reconnaissance targets are rare in this fleet (e.g., Approval Management).
config.expected_signal: Portals like 'Microsoft Approval Management' showing very low user counts. An actor hitting these is more likely to be anomalous.

primitive_config.label: Rare Discovery Portal Baseline
primitive_config.content: SELECT dst_endpoint_name, COUNT(DISTINCT actor_user_name) as users, MIN(time) as first_seen FROM hb_auth_signin WHERE status_id = 1 AND instr(',' || '{{discovery_portals}}' || ',', ',' || LOWER(dst_endpoint_name) || ',') > 0 AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days') GROUP BY dst_endpoint_name ORDER BY users ASC
primitive_config.expected: Portals like 'Microsoft Approval Management' showing very low user counts. An actor hitting these is more likely to be anomalous.

config.content: SELECT actor_user_name, COUNT(*) as touch_count, COUNT(DISTINCT file_path) as unique_files, MIN(time) as first_touch, MAX(time) as last_touch FROM hb_file_activity WHERE provider = 'm365' AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days') GROUP BY actor_user_name HAVING unique_files > 50 ORDER BY unique_files DESC
config.description: Identify users with unusually high volumes of file access in SharePoint/OneDrive, consistent with automated collection.
config.expected_signal: Users performing massive file enumeration. Correlating these users with those in the portal sequence suggests an automated drain.

primitive_config.label: M365 High-Volume File Activity
primitive_config.content: SELECT actor_user_name, COUNT(*) as touch_count, COUNT(DISTINCT file_path) as unique_files, MIN(time) as first_touch, MAX(time) as last_touch FROM hb_file_activity WHERE provider = 'm365' AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days') GROUP BY actor_user_name HAVING unique_files > 50 ORDER BY unique_files DESC
primitive_config.expected: Users performing massive file enumeration. Correlating these users with those in the portal sequence suggests an automated drain.

config.content: SELECT device_hostname, query_hostname, COUNT(*) as query_count, MIN(time) as first_seen FROM hb_dns_activity WHERE instr(',' || '{{phishing_domains}}' || ',', '.' || LOWER(query_hostname) || ',') > 0 OR instr(',' || '{{phishing_domains}}' || ',', LOWER(query_hostname) || ',') > 0 AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days') GROUP BY device_hostname, query_hostname
config.description: Correlate portal access and file activity with host-level DNS lookups to the phishing infrastructure named in the research.
config.expected_signal: A host-to-domain match. This provides high-confidence evidence that the identity compromise originated from the specific social engineering campaign.

config.objective: Determine if any user shows a pattern of successful portal reconnaissance (3+ portals) followed by high-volume file activity, especially if correlated with phishing domain lookups.
